newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude prices fall with WTI, Mayan sold.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude prices fall with WTI, Mayan sold.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices fell Monday, reflecting news that Iraq and the United Nations finalized a plan allowing the key Middle East oil exporter to resume shipments within a month, traders said.

Meanwhile, sales of Alaska North Slope (ANs) crude -- the regional benchmark -- remained stagnant, with important buyers in the Pacific Northwest oversupplied with gasoline and unwilling to pay BP's current offer of $1.85 under WTI.

Discounts for ANS remained $2.16 a barrel under WTI. With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude fell to $16.71/16.87 a barrel, in line with lower cash prices for West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude.
Another light crude, Line 63, also fell with WTI, while its discount remained steady at $3.05 a barrel, and its price over Buena Vista stood unchanged at 90 cents to $1.00.
State-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) sold a 360,000 barrel cargo of Mayan heavy crude to a Los Angeles refinery late last week, market sources said Monday.
The crude, which is high in hydrogen sulphide, has been kept from southern California markets since 1991 due to the region's strict refinery emission rules.
Traders said the grade could displace California's Point Arguello crude, which has similar viscosity and sulphur content.
Meanwhile, Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- fell after major oil companies lowered postings late Monday.
